chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Basheer, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ahmasy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Abu Saeed asked him about the qamis (gown), and I was in his presence, its warp being of silk: 'Can one wear it?' He was feeling cold, so he instructed him to wear it.

key_terms.الْخَمِيصَة: A type of long shirt or gown
key_terms.يَلْبَسُهَا: To wear it (referring to the garment)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for men to wear silk clothing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'al-maslahah' (public interest/benefit) in Shia jurisprudence, where the general prohibition of silk for men is relaxed for medical or practical necessity, such as alleviating cold. The specific mention of the narrator's presence and the Imam's personal state underscores the contextual nature of this ruling, distinguishing it from a blanket permission for all silk garments.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Abu Al Hassan Al Ahmasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Abu Saeed asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the gown, and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, its hemming being of silk, can one wear it and he was feeling cold?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> instructed him that he can wear it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindy from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from abu al-Hassan al-Ahmasiy who has said the following:

“Abu Sa‘id once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Khamisah (a square-shaped gown with prints), when I was there, with its warp of abrisam (silk from silk worm); if it can be used in very cold weather. He (the Imam) commanded him to wear it.’”
